newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Volvo upped to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Volvo upped to hold.

text.p: -- Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Monday it had upgraded its rating for Swedish auto maker AB Volvo's American Depositary Receipts (ADR) to hold from sell.
-- "The company should demonstrate solid operating profit momentum going forward," analyst Juergen Pieper wrote.
-- "We see operating profits (EBIT) progressing as follows: 1996E $332 million, 1997E $660 million and 1998E $936 million."
-- Pieper raised his estimates for earnings per ADR to $2.47 from $1.40 in 1997 and to $1.98 from $1.64 in 1998.

-- "Not all of the significant increase in the 1997 estimate is attributable to improved operating performance; Volvo continues to sell off non-core assets so earnings per share are influenced by capital gains."

-- "... Volvo's auto division, which we had believed would hurt the company's performance in 1997, is doing well. The new 40 Series is selling strongly. Moreover, the company expects cost savings of $75 million from headcount reduction in autos."
-- The company's stock opened up 1/4 to 21-7/8 in New York.
